messages:
Incident Bot: Pager triggered for cluster-gpu-7: high rate of NCCL ALLREDUCE timeouts, multiple task pods crashing. Severity: P1. @Raj (oncall) paged.

Raj (oncall): taking.

Raj (oncall): seeing a bunch of repeats: `nccl: unhandled exception` in job job-Atlas-2145 (pipeline-parallel, TP=2). Pods flapping with CUDA OOM then communicator reset.

Emily K.: jumping in. which node group? any node flaps in cloud?

Raj (oncall): cluster-gpu-7, nodes g7-3,g7-4 show container restarts around 2143456550. last kube event: OOMKilled -> container restart -> nccl timeout.

Infra-Bot: Node g7-3 reported GPU driver reprobe at 2143456602. NIC health OK.

Mike H.: logs from one of the failed pods:
```
2026-03-15T21:02:33Z model-worker | CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
2026-03-15T21:02:33Z model-worker | ncclcomm.cpp:292 NCCL ERROR "unhandled system error" (NCCL_ERR_UNSUPPORTED)
2026-03-15T21:02:34Z model-worker | killing process: aborting job
```

Sara L.: is this during the allreduce step on micro-batches? sounds like memory blow up + communicator inconsistent state.

Raj (oncall): yes, TP stage boundary - we saw buffer allocation spikes. Affected jobs: job-Atlas-2145 (prod-training), job-int-912 (internal repro), batch inference pool briefly impacted.

Emily K.: customer-facing impact? Atlas AI has one active training run; they're seeing intermittent job failures and slow retries. Recommend we notify CS with RCA-in-progress.

Raj (oncall): noted. @Ops Oncall can you prepare a short customer blurb?

Ops Oncall: Will do. Draft: "We're investigating multi-GPU training interruptions affecting a small number of jobs. We're actively mitigating and will update in 30m."

Mike H.: mitigation plan attempt 1: try graceful communicator restart + drain node g7-3. Steps I'm running now: `kubectl cordon g7-3 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then restart agent on g7-3.

Infra-Bot: drain started for g7-3 at 2143456710. Pod eviction in progress.

Raj (oncall): while pods reschedule, we should reduce TP degree for the impacted job(s) to avoid cross-node collectives that hit NCCL. Can we patch job-Atlas-2145 to TP=1 as a temporary fallback? That will slow training but should stabilize.

Emily K.: Agree. Triggering a rolling-update for job-Atlas-2145 with env override: `REDWOOD_TP_DEGREE=1`. Also set `REDWOOD_NCCL_ASYNC_FALLBACK=1` so runtime will auto-fallback communicator strategy on reset (experimental).

Mike H.: applied patch to job-Atlas-2145 at 2143456812. New pods coming up on same node group but with TP=1 config.

Sara L.: still seeing one pod crash with CUDA OOM on g7-4 at 2143456850. Might be residual memory leak in the model code when re-initializing buffers. Need to kill hung communicator processes too.

Mike H.: running `pkill -f nccl` on g7-4 to clear stale communicators, then restarting runtime agent.

Infra-Bot: agent restart on g7-4 completed at 2143456899. No driver reprobe.

Raj (oncall): good. job-Atlas-2145 pods stabilized on TP=1; no further NCCL errors in the last 3 rounds. job-int-912 still failing occasionally, collecting more logs.

Emily K.: collecting core dumps and GPU traces for dev. Mike, can you upload `dmesg`/`nvidia-smi -q` outputs to the incident artifact bucket? Put path in thread.

Mike H.: uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/2143456789/g7-3-logs.tar.gz and g7-4-logs.tar.gz. Added kernel oops and driver logs.

Sara L.: quick triage notes: sequence looks like 1) buffer allocation spike at allreduce boundary -> CUDA OOM on some ranks, 2) those ranks abort -> NCCL reports communicator failure -> other ranks hang waiting -> kubernetes kills pods (OOMKilled or CrashLoop). Contributing factor: host-level driver reprobe on g7-3 earlier which may have desynced NIC/GPU state.

Raj (oncall): mitigations applied: drained g7-3, restarted agent on g7-4, temporary TP downgrade for customer job, set experimental NCCL fallback flag. Next: schedule full node soak test, run driver sanity across g7 fleet, and add runtime guard to detect OOM during allreduce and trigger local fallback (queueing/prefetch reduction) instead of global hang.

Emily K.: agree. Production followups (owners):
- Infra: driver & node reprobe root cause (owner: Mike H.)
- Runtime: implement OOM-during-collective guard and async fallback (owner: Sara L.)
- Product/CS: customer comms and credits for Atlas AI (owner: Emily K.)

Raj (oncall): customer impact note for PSR: job-Atlas-2145 experienced ~18 minutes interruption with automatic fallback to TP=1; no data lost, checkpoints valid. ETA to full restore (TP=2) after driver validation: 6h.

Ops Oncall: customer blurb sent to Atlas SRE and CSchannel at 2143457180.

Mike H.: opening follow-up ticket INF-1019 to run gpu driver stress and NIC validation on g7 nodes; attaching logs.

Infra-Bot: INF-1019 created.

Sara L.: we'll add an immediate runtime guard in canary (staging) to catch large allocation growth during collectives and force a local-kick fallback. I'll push a patch to canary tomorrow morning.

Raj (oncall): closing immediate pager: system stabilized after drain and restarts. Leaving this thread open for postmortem notes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Incident Bot: Pager resolved at 2143457420 (no active alarms)."
